Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Quick answers at a high level so Harbor can decide next steps: 

- Contractual addendum: Yes, Redwood can work from a GLBA-focused addendum. Our legal team prefers to start from our standard DPA + a GLBA exhibit, then iterate.
- US-only residency: We can offer US-only data residency for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers today. For Hosted accounts, we have region restrictions (US-only tenancy) and can provide contractual assurances, plus an audited subprocessors list.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current CSV. We classify access levels (metadata-only vs. content-access). No external subprocessors have access to model training processes by default; we do not use customer content for model training unless explicitly contracted.
- Retention & logs: We can meet 7-year retention for audit logs via our retention add-on; for application data we recommend a mutually agreed retention policy.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood legal drafts a GLBA addendum (we can turn around a first draft in ~7 business days once we have the questionnaire completed).
2) Mutual action plan for pilot (incl. dates, environment type — Hosted vs Dedicated).
3) Security call to walk Harbor's InfoSec through subprocessors, KMS, and access controls.

I'm looping in Neha (legal) and Laura (solutions) to scope the addendum and timelines. Marcus

—Marcus Lin

Marcus / Laura — reviewed Harbor's questionnaire and the ask. Summary of legal position and recommended approach: 

1) Residency & Deployment: Recommend Redwood propose Dedicated (reserved capacity) for the pilot to meet Harbor's "no non-US subprocessors" desire. We can also support Hosted with US-only tenancy but must carve an explicit contractual clause that disallows cross-border subprocessors for Harbor-controlled data. Dedicated gives stronger operational guarantees and simplifies audits.

2) Subprocessors: Provide current inventory (attached) and include contractual covenants prohibiting cross-border transfers for Harbor data. Add a right-to-approve future subprocessors for GLBA-scoped data (reasonable consent).

3) Retention & Logs: Accept Harbor's 7-year retention for audit logs; propose Redwood will retain immutable audit trails for at least 7 years under our observability add-on (costed). Application-level data retention should be contractually configurable per Harbor's instructions.

4) Key clauses to include in draft addendum: definitions (GLBA-protected info), purpose/processing, residency, subprocessors & approvals, security measures (KMS, encryption at rest/in transit), breach notification (48-72 hours), right-to-audit, indemnity cap carveouts for privacy breaches involving insured PII. Also include a short operational exhibit describing the pilot environment (nodes, region, isolation).

5) Timeline: If Harbor returns the completed questionnaire this week, Redwood can circulate a draft addendum by 2026-11-21. Legal will be available for a joint call the week of 11/22.

Attaching: Redwood_GLBA_Draft_Addendum_v1.docx and redwood-subprocessor-list-20261114.csv (inventory with access tiers). 

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
